A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research study with complete main text and Appendices A–H. Text comparison and rendered-page checks support reliable comparison of the equations, figures, tables, and appendices.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmarking experiments across six QA datasets, including QA performance, computational efficiency, self-knowledge, OOD transfer, and uncertainty-method analyses in Sections 5–7 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–2 and the detailed experiments and analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The retrieval procedures, uncertainty methods, Hybrid feature combination, classifiers, and model adaptations described in Sections 3–4 and Appendices F–G are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use NQ, SQuAD, TriviaQA, MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and 2WikiMultiHopQA, with identical cross-dataset OOD coverage. Wikipedia retrieval data and supplementary C4 training data are also unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in corresponding experiments, including IRCoT, AdaptiveRAG, DRAGIN, FLARE, Rowen variants, SeaKR, uncertainty methods, and FS-RAG in appendix Tables 7–8.

E3.justification: The model configurations, 500-question test subsets, prompts, classifier settings, and evaluation metrics are unchanged. Apparent numerical edits are superscript footnote renumbering: Elasticsearch remains 7.17.9, and IRCoT retains eight iterations and a 15-paragraph limit.

E4.justification: Classifier sensitivity, OOD robustness, functional complexity, Hybrid feature importance, and metric-correlation analyses retain the same questions and evidence in Sections 6–7 and Appendices A, D, E, and H.

E5.justification: Both retain 1,000 bootstrap rounds in Appendix F, the same standard-deviation reporting in Tables 5–8, and Friedman and Nemenyi tests in Appendix B. No run-count, seed, or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results, rankings, and findings match throughout the main text and appendices, including the fine-tuned baseline results in Table 15. For example, Table 1 reports EigValLaplacian's NQ In-Accuracy as 0.512 in both versions.

T1.justification: The self-knowledge definitions in Section 4.3.3 and the Rademacher-complexity and Hessian-sharpness formulations in Section 7 are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, three contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same study scope and claims concerning uncertainty methods' QA performance, efficiency, self-knowledge, transferability, and complexity.

C2.justification: Interpretations of performance differences, OOD degradation, and functional complexity are unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning evaluation with one primary language model and six QA datasets.

D1.justification: On page 2, v1 promises that data and code will be published soon. v2 states that all code and data are published and adds a footnote identifying the GitHub repository s-nlp/AdaRAGUE. This updates availability and access information; implementation disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work, the bibliography, method citations, and positioning relative to previous research are unchanged. The added repository reference concerns this work's own resources.

P1.justification: The code/data availability sentence is rewritten and the arXiv version/date stamp is updated. The remaining prose and organization of sections and appendices are unchanged.

P2.justification: The new repository footnote causes limited column reflow on page 2 and renumbers subsequent footnotes. Figures, tables, captions, and their placement are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Replacing a future-release promise with a concrete code/data repository reference modestly improves the paper's reproducibility information. The scientific content and supporting evidence are unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's completeness or usability, so the supported improvement is limited.
